subject.title: [Feature]: Granular session visibility — split tools.sessions.visibility into per-capability knobs

question: Should OpenClaw add a per-capability `tools.sessions.visibility` object, or should cross-agent send/read/list separation be handled by the existing A2A allowlist, per-agent visibility, and allowlist proposals?
rationale: The request changes the transcript privacy boundary and public config shape, and active related proposals overlap the same session authorization surface without one settled model.

options.title: Approve unified capability object
options.body: Adopt a backward-compatible object form for send, history, list, and metadata after reconciling it with allowlist, per-agent, sandbox, and A2A semantics.

options.title: Use adjacent policy axes instead
options.body: Make the open allowlist, per-agent A2A, or send-only proposals canonical if maintainers decide those satisfy the send-without-read privacy goal better than per-capability flags.

options.title: Keep current fail-closed model
options.body: Continue requiring broad visibility for cross-agent session tools and document the privacy-versus-coordination tradeoff as intentional for now.

recommendation.title: Approve unified capability object
recommendation.body: Adopt a backward-compatible object form for send, history, list, and metadata after reconciling it with allowlist, per-agent, sandbox, and A2A semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The current shared session-tool authorization and config boundary traces most clearly to this history, and the remaining choice is a security/product policy decision on that surface.
